cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Fresh users now land on the Research → Plan → Implement workflow in the New Task form instead of Freeform.
cards.claim: HumanLayer made Research-Plan-Implement the default workflow for new tasks on 2026-06-06, replacing Freeform.
cards.landing: Ship plan section 0 phase routine; confirms staged-phase default

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: A fast first draft does not save time when its design is wrong.
cards.claim: Because agents write code faster than people review it, review is the bottleneck, so cheap review of short planning documents should precede large diffs.
cards.landing: Phase routine: draft PR plan-first, review the plan before the code

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Choose the shortest path that addresses the main risk
cards.claim: Not every task needs every phase; pick the shortest workflow (Oneshot, RPI, PRD-oriented, Freeform) that covers the main risk, sized by task.
cards.evidence_detail: Guidance; 0.183.0 also added a new-task box suggesting a workflow by task size.
cards.landing: Ship plan: tier phases by risk so small phases skip the full routine

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: It does not pick a future design, so reviewers can correct facts before they become design assumptions.
cards.claim: Research phase only describes the current system (code, tests, named sources) and never proposes a design, so facts are reviewed separately from decisions.
cards.landing: Cold-resume trial and knowledge store: separate verified current-state facts from decisions

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: The agent can propose a choice, but the user owns the decision.
cards.claim: Agents must not make product or design choices; design discussions keep each choice open until the user answers clearly, and PRD/TDD need explicit approvals.
cards.landing: Phase routine decisions journal and owner-view: explicit decision checkpoints

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Vertical slices, which connect only what one result needs.
cards.claim: Structure outlines should split work into vertical slices each ending runnable, visible or queryable (e.g. fixed API data verified with curl first), not horizontal layers.
cards.landing: Ship plan phase design: each of the 40 phases names one testable result and its checks

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Later artifacts take priority over earlier ones, but current code is the source of truth
cards.claim: When artifacts conflict, later ones win, but live code beats any document for questions of current behavior.
cards.evidence_detail: Precedence order: plan > outline > TDD > PRD > design > research > ticket.
cards.landing: CLAUDE.md/doc drift rule and cold-resume trial: code over prose

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Feedback on a structure outline changes the outline and does not start implementation.
cards.claim: Feedback on planning artifacts revises the document only and never triggers implementation; implementation pauses after each phase for manual review by default.
cards.landing: Phase routine: review gate between plan revision and implementation

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Auto-advance does not create a duplicate newer phase.
cards.claim: Auto-advance covers only safe handoffs (questions to research, research to design, plan to implement, implement to PR) and never design to outline or outline to implementation; each transition turns itself off after running.
cards.evidence_detail: Rule list; auto-advance first appears in 0.117.3 fix and 0.115.0 Linear auto-advance.
cards.landing: Phase routine: which handoffs may be unattended vs gated on owner

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Create commands write a new numbered artifact. Iterate commands edit an existing one in place.
cards.claim: Each phase has a create-* and iterate-* skill pair (22 rpi: skills); creates write numbered artifacts, iterates edit in place and are not separate phases.
cards.landing: Skills under .claude/skills/: create/iterate pairing per artifact type

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Outline implementation never calls `create-plan` or `implement-plan`.
cards.claim: Each artifact owns one concern (research=findings, design=options, PRD=what/why, TDD=how, outline=phases, PR description=review summary) and implementation modes are strictly separated.
cards.landing: Ship plan artifacts: one-concern-per-document rule

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: describe-pr ... reviews the full diff against the task artifacts
cards.claim: describe-pr is the final agent phase: it commits and pushes, reviews the whole diff against the task artifacts, writes the description, and adds an HTML walkthrough only for 300+ lines across 5+ files.
cards.landing: Per-PR Opus reviewer step and PR body template; size-gated extras

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: /rpi:describe-pr now watches checks, fixes failures caused by the PR, and asks for approval
cards.claim: The PR skill now watches CI checks, fixes failures it caused, and asks approval before resolving merge conflicts.
cards.landing: Closing step of phase routine: CI-watch and fix loop with approval for conflicts

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Use /hl:orchestrate to break down work, launch tasks in separate worktrees, start sessions
cards.claim: /hl:orchestrate skill breaks work into tasks in separate worktrees, starts sessions, checks task and PR status, and moves artifacts between tasks; 0.183.0 adds auto-advance defaults per workflow and a workflow chart.
cards.landing: Saved workflow library: an orchestrator skill that fans a plan out to per-phase sessions

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: The new /hl:teleport skill guides an agent through saving your work, setting up a remote host
cards.claim: /hl:teleport moves a task to another machine by saving work and starting a new session there on the same task; 0.183.0 has it update CLI, Claude Code and gh on the new host.
cards.landing: Cold-resume: task state recoverable on a fresh machine from artifacts alone

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Move a session from Claude Code to Codex, or back.
cards.claim: Sessions can be handed off between Claude Code and Codex, continuing on the same task and worktree with the full transcript.
cards.landing: Harness portability: keep instructions in AGENTS.md-compatible form; cross-agent verifier

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Your organization's engineering knowledge compounds across sessions.
cards.claim: Context Shards plus Compounding Engineering shipped in early access, a cross-session organizational knowledge store (no mechanism described).
cards.evidence_detail: One line, opt-in via Slack or email; no details.
cards.landing: Knowledge-store pilot design: comparable product exists but mechanism unpublished

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Codex subagents now fork from the caller's context instead of starting cold
cards.claim: Fork-mode subagents inherit the caller's context rather than starting cold, and subagents can be resumed after finishing, erroring or interruption.
cards.landing: Subagent design: fork vs cold start for verifiers and refuters (refuters need cold; implementers may fork)

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: CodeLayer subagents now delegate at most three levels deep
cards.claim: Subagent nesting is capped at three levels to stop fork chains spawning runaway agents.
cards.landing: Workflow-tool scripts: depth cap on nested agents

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Large web search and fetch results are truncated so one lookup can't crowd out the rest
cards.claim: Web search and fetch results are truncated so one lookup cannot consume the session context.
cards.landing: Output caps on tool results in Workflow scripts and readers

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Workspaces pin to the exact commit from their first successful setup
cards.claim: Workspaces pin the exact commit of first setup so a task moved to another machine rebuilds from the same source rather than a moved branch.
cards.landing: Phase routine: draft PR body 'Plan @ <sha>' pinning; cold-resume reproducibility

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: No RPI sub-agent uses a fixed Opus model.
cards.claim: RPI research sub-agents (locator, analyzer, pattern-finder) use Sonnet (or Haiku via an experiment), the implementer and reviewer use Sonnet, and only the outline implementer inherits the parent model.
cards.landing: .claude/agents: Haiku locator already matches; consider Sonnet analyzer/reviewer split

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: HumanLayer does not add an RPI-specific Claude effort setting.
cards.claim: Sub-agent effort is not specially set: it follows the session's thinking setting or model default (an Opus child with none set ran at medium in one SDK test); on Codex most children run at low effort and only the outline implementer inherits parent effort.
cards.evidence_detail: One SDK test noted, no numbers.
cards.landing: Verifier effort routing: default children low/medium, reserve high for implementer

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: code search speed and cost are more important than Sonnet's added analysis
cards.claim: Faster Research Subagents (Haiku for the three codebase research agents) is an opt-in trade of analysis depth for speed and cost.
cards.evidence_detail: Experiment toggle; org and user must both allow.
cards.landing: Existing Haiku fixflow-explorer; cost routing for read-only agents

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Research delegation stays within the listed specialist roster, avoiding expensive parent model inheritance.
cards.claim: RPI research skills were fixed to delegate only to the listed specialist agents because falling back to general agents inherited the expensive parent model.
cards.evidence_detail: Bug fix note; implies a real cost leak.
cards.landing: Custom agents with pinned model; forbid generic-agent fallback in scripts

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: The outline implementer sub-agent now inherits the parent session's reasoning effort instead of always running at low effort.
cards.claim: The outline-implementer sub-agent had been forced to low effort and was changed to inherit the parent's effort, i.e. low effort was too weak for implementation.
cards.landing: Effort routing: implementers inherit; read-only/verification children can be lower

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Codex research sub-agents now run on Terra X high instead of the session's larger root model.
cards.claim: Codex research sub-agents were moved off the larger root model to a mid-tier model at high effort.
cards.landing: Model routing for research children

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: you MUST NOT launch it in the background.
cards.claim: The harness injects a prompt rule that sub-agents must never run in the background, never use resume, and never set the model unless the user asks.
cards.landing: Workflow/agent conventions: forbid model override and background runs in subagents

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: may only be edited using the explicit write and edit tools
cards.claim: Task artifacts are reached through a symlinked directory and the agent is told to edit them only with explicit write/edit tools, not Bash sed/python, so the sync layer sees every change.
cards.landing: Observability of compliance: route evidence writes through tools that can be logged (a partial hook substitute)

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: The agent checks the artifacts directory first.
cards.claim: When the user asks to continue a task or an rpi: skill without naming a file, the injected prompt tells the agent to look in the task artifacts directory first, i.e. resume from stored artifacts.
cards.landing: Cold-resume trial: a fixed first-look location the agent is told to consult

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Uses the first non-empty file from AGENTS.md, then CLAUDE.md.
cards.claim: Instruction files from every repo in a multi-repo workspace are loaded under a 'Repository Instructions' header; 0.124.1 loads layered global, repo-root and working-directory instructions with .local.md overrides, and 0.149.0 prefers AGENTS.md over CLAUDE.md.
cards.landing: CLAUDE.md trim: nested per-directory instruction files rather than one 390-line root file

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Setup may still be running, but the agent can start working.
cards.claim: If workspace setup steps are running, failed or skipped, the session prompt lists each with its status and stderr so the agent knows its environment state.
cards.landing: Phase-start environment status block (what ran, what failed) in session preamble

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Record all current decisions in the artifact before switching sessions.
cards.claim: At a phase boundary, record all decisions in the artifact, then either update in-session if context remains or start a fresh session with the matching iterate skill when context is nearly out.
cards.landing: One phase per new chat; decisions journal as the hand-off carrier

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: A task can contain several sessions.
cards.claim: Research, design, implementation and review each run in their own session sharing one task whose files live in a synced task directory (10 MB text limit per file), so a fresh session loses no history.
cards.landing: Evidence folder / task-directory as the cross-session memory carrier

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Later agent work can read reviewer comments
cards.claim: Reviewer comments on artifacts are readable by later agent work, and a review-artifact-comments skill acts on comments one at a time, so review feedback is machine-consumable.
cards.evidence_detail: Docs; Release 0.141.0 adds sending artifact threads back to the agent.
cards.landing: Owner view: comments on plan files fed back to the next session

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Automation runs reuse one task per automation
cards.claim: A CLI runs one scoped coding session inside CI with permission prompts bypassed, exits with a code reflecting the result, and reuses one task per automation; recurring agents use a no-op guard (exit if an open agent PR exists), a concurrency group, and a repo markdown memory file.
cards.evidence_detail: Guide with GitHub Actions example; 0.166.0 calls it experimental.
cards.landing: Scheduled routines: one-unreviewed-PR-at-a-time guard and memory file in repo

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: /iterate comment on an agent PR reruns the agent on the same branch with the feedback
cards.claim: A PR comment trigger (/iterate) reruns the agent on the same branch with the feedback, giving a review-to-fix loop driven from GitHub.
cards.landing: Saved workflow: comment-triggered iterate on draft PRs

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: A local value replaces a shared value. A shared value replaces the built-in default.
cards.claim: Workspace setup is layered: built-in defaults, committed workspace.json, uncommitted workspace.local.json; array fields append, repo entries merge by path.
cards.landing: Settings layering for .claude (shared vs local) and worktree-per-phase config

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: a task started on a directory now runs in its own worktrees instead of editing your checkout
cards.claim: Tasks now run in their own worktrees by default (with an opt-out), and the daemon hides its .shadow folder from git so agents do not commit it.
cards.landing: One worktree per phase; exclude tool state dirs from git

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Dismissing the context window warning hides it in every session for 7 days
cards.claim: Context-window warnings are model-aware (0.105.0), 0.182.0 adds an always-visible context meter, and 0.180.0 lets users dismiss the warning, showing context budget is surfaced as a UI signal.
cards.evidence_detail: Several changelog lines (0.105.0, 0.180.0, 0.182.0); Codex gauge corrected to ~258k real window in 0.122.1.
cards.landing: Context budget monitoring: use real window size per model, not marketed 1M

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: clarifying questions and pushback continue the conversation instead of rewriting the doc on every message
cards.claim: PRD/TDD skills run an interview loop that settles one decision before editing the document, and the TDD interview defaults to a code block per option (0.115.0) so options are compared as actual shapes.
cards.landing: Design-discussion skill: one decision per message, options shown as code

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: ranks every task by token spend or cost
cards.claim: Advanced Metrics ranks tasks by token spend or cost and splits by agent, model, stage, person or mode, with workflow spend compared in ranked lists.
cards.landing: Measurement pipeline (skipped): per-stage token and cost attribution

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Claude subprocesses are stopped on archive/delete and reaped after 10 minutes idle
cards.claim: Idle Claude processes are reaped after 10 minutes and sessions that hit a usage limit resume on their own after reset.
cards.landing: Workflow-tool runs: idle and limit handling for long scripts

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: the session keeps going on the backup model
cards.claim: A model refusal that triggered a fallback (Fable 5 to Opus 4.8) used to kill the session and lose the conversation; fallback is now surfaced inline and persists.
cards.landing: Workflow scripts: explicit fallback model on refusal, not session loss

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Selecting Opus 4.8 now switches to Claude Code's safer auto mode automatically
cards.claim: Selecting Opus 4.8 switches sessions to Claude Code's auto permission mode by default, and the research-questions skill captures user-given links and file paths verbatim in a 'Key Context Pointers' section (same release).
cards.landing: Permission mode choice per phase; research-question skill keeps owner pointers verbatim

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Claude Code subagents can now invoke workflow skills.
cards.claim: Subagents can invoke workflow skills; Claude Code is the only supported harness for Anthropic models; 0.140.0 fixed Codex 5.6 invoking skills overeagerly.
cards.landing: Skills design: whether subagents may call skills; guard against over-eager skill use

gaps: Docs subpages were read only through WebFetch small-model summaries, not raw text; quotes from them are taken from the summaries and may be paraphrased rather than verbatim page text, and the system-prompt-additions tool refused to give verbatim prompt blocks.

docs.humanlayer.com release notes before 0.101.7 and the pages for tutorials, remote daemons, Bedrock, LLM gateway, Slack, Linear, Jira and the workspace-config reference were not read (outside bundle list).
Context Shards and Compounding Engineering have only a one-line description; no mechanism published.
Authorship: docs and release notes are unsigned product copy; authored as Dex+others by assumption, none attributable to Dex personally.
Release dates for docs subpages are estimated from the release note that mentions them; WebFetch gave no page dates.
